attacker.model: claude (Kiro subagent; exact model version not exposed to the agent)

notApplicable.null-vs-empty: The only input is an int; no text input exists. A NULL value is already a fixed case (REPLICATE with a NULL length is NULL).
notApplicable.collation-case: No text input; the result is never compared as text.
notApplicable.trailing-spaces: No text input; CONVERT(varchar(8), int) never adds spaces.
notApplicable.numeric-rounding: The input is an int; no decimal or money value.
notApplicable.top-ties: Scalar function: returns one value, no rows from tables.
notApplicable.identity-gaps: Reads no table, no key or sequence.

cases.label: -1000 (5 characters with the sign) gets three zeros before the sign: '000-1000'
cases.reasoning: T-SQL pads the string '-1000' with REPLICATE('0', 8 - DATALENGTH) on the left, so the zeros go before the sign. A to_char or lpad of abs() with a leading sign would give '-0001000'. The hand-derived cases use negative values of 2, 8, 9 and 11 characters only; 5 characters is a length class none of them uses.

cases.label: -100000 (7 characters with the sign) gets one zero before the sign: '0-100000'
cases.reasoning: One character short of the exact fit for a negative value: REPLICATE('0', 1) goes before the sign. A length test that counted digits only (6) would pad two zeros; one that tested abs(value) against 8 digits would keep it unpadded. No hand-derived case uses a 7-character negative value.

cases.label: -999999999 (10 characters with the sign) does not fit varchar(8): '0000000*'
cases.reasoning: 9 digits and 10 characters with the sign. A check on the number of digits against 9 (the positive overflow boundary) or a substring of the text would keep part of it; SQL Server's CONVERT(varchar(8)) gives '*'. The hand-derived negative overflow cases are 9 and 11 characters; 10 characters is a class none of them uses.

cases.label: 1000 (4 digits) gets four leading zeros: '00001000'
cases.reasoning: A mid-range length: REPLICATE('0', 4). A conversion computing the pad width from log10(value) or from integer division would be off by one on an exact power of ten. The hand-derived positive cases use 1, 8, 9 and 10 characters; 4 characters is a class none of them uses.

cases.label: 9999999 (7 digits) gets one leading zero: '09999999'
cases.reasoning: One below the 8-digit boundary; REPLICATE('0', 1). An integer-division or log10-based length would be off by one here.

cases.label: -10 keeps its sign inside the padding: '00000-10'
cases.reasoning: Two-digit negative value; checks that the sign counts as one character of the 8 (DATALENGTH of varchar counts bytes, one per ASCII character).

cases.label: 100000 (6 digits, an exact power of ten) gets two leading zeros: '00100000'
cases.reasoning: Exact power of ten with 6 digits: floor(log10(100000)) + 1 = 6, but a ceil(log10()) length gives 5 and pads three zeros. No hand-derived case uses a 6-character value.

cases.label: -10000 (6 characters with the sign) gets two zeros before the sign: '00-10000'
cases.reasoning: A 6-character negative value; the sign is one of the 8 characters (DATALENGTH of varchar counts one byte per ASCII character), so two zeros are added before the sign. No hand-derived case uses a 6-character negative value.
